_doc: Guide v2 content for /guides/ai-3d-model-to-engine/. Every step is written from the linked official docs (checked 2026-10-17). Videos must be from the vendor's/project's own YouTube channel (verified via oEmbed). Images only with a clear reuse licence, stored in src/assets/guides/<slug>/.
result: A clean, game-ready mesh (right scale, fixed normals, sensible polycount, baked normal map) in Unreal, Unity or Godot with its textures intact.

do: Before generating, look up what your generator plan lets you do with the output.
Meshy Free: CC BY 4.0, so you can sell games using it if you credit Meshy. Paid Meshy plans give you private, customer-owned assets.
Tripo Free: Tripo keeps the rights and doesn't grant commercial use. A paid plan gives you commercial rights.
shared.see: You know whether you can ship the model and what credit line, if any, it needs.
shared.gotcha: Summaries of Tripo's free tier online contradict each other, so go by Tripo's own help centre and terms.

source.label: Tripo: can I use models commercially?

shared.h: Generate and export GLB or FBX
do: In Meshy, click Download and pick GLB (one file with textures inside) or FBX (better for rigs and animation).
Turn on Quad Mesh in Meshy if you'll retopologise or rig, and set a target polycount with Remesh if you want.
In Tripo, export GLB or FBX the same way.
shared.see: A single .glb file, or an .fbx with its texture files.
shared.gotcha: GLB stores triangles, so quads are lost. Export FBX or OBJ if you need to keep quads.

shared.h: Import into Blender and clean up
do: Use File > Import > glTF 2.0 (.glb/.gltf), or File > Import > FBX.
In Object Mode, apply rotation and scale with Object > Apply > Rotation & Scale (Ctrl-A).
In Edit Mode, select everything and run Mesh > Merge > By Distance to weld duplicate vertices.
Run Mesh > Normals > Recalculate Outside (Shift-N).
shared.see: Scale reads 1, 1, 1, and the Face Orientation overlay shows no red (back-facing) patches.
shared.gotcha: Applying a negative scale flips faces; tick Corrective Flip Normals in the Apply options to fix it.

do: Add a Decimate modifier in Collapse mode and lower Ratio until you reach the face count you want.
For cleaner, even topology, use Properties > Data > Remesh in Voxel or Quad (QuadriFlow) mode instead.
Keep a copy of the original high-poly mesh: you'll bake its detail in the next step.
shared.see: The modifier shows the new face count and the silhouette still looks right.
shared.gotcha: Remesh ignores modifiers and won't run on an object with a Multiresolution modifier.

shared.h: UV unwrap and bake the detail
do: Remeshing removes the original UVs, so in Edit Mode run UV > Unwrap > Smart UV Project on the low-poly mesh.
In the low-poly material, add an Image Texture node with a new image and leave it selected.
Switch to Cycles, and under Render > Bake set Bake Type to Normal and turn on Selected to Active.
Select the high-poly mesh, then Shift-select the low-poly one so it's active, and click Bake.
shared.see: A normal map on the low-poly mesh that brings back the high-poly detail.
shared.gotcha: If parts of the bake come out blank, raise Extrusion or Max Ray Distance, or use a cage.

do: For glTF: File > Export > glTF 2.0, Format glTF Binary (.glb), with Selected Objects, Apply Modifiers and +Y Up on.
For FBX: File > Export > FBX (.fbx) with Selected Objects and Apply Modifiers on.
For engines that expect Y-up FBX, set Forward to -Z and Up to Y.
shared.see: One file that re-imports at the right size and facing the right way.
shared.gotcha: The FBX exporter's Apply Transform option is experimental and can break rigs and animation.

do: Drag the .glb or .fbx into the Content Browser, or click Import there.
In the import options, enable Build Nanite under Static Meshes if you want Nanite.
Click Import.
steps.see: A static mesh asset with its materials and textures in the Content Browser.
steps.gotcha: If it arrives the wrong size or rotated, adjust the uniform scale or rotation offset in the import options.

do: FBX is Unity's main model format: drag it into your Assets folder.
For GLB, first install glTFast: in Package Manager, add a package by name and enter com.unity.cloud.gltfast.
Select the model and set Scale Factor or Convert Units on the Inspector's Model tab.
On the Materials tab, choose a material creation mode and extract textures if you need to edit them.
steps.see: A model prefab at 1 unit = 1 metre with its materials applied.
steps.gotcha: For .gltf (not .glb), copy the .bin and image files too and don't rename them, or the references break.

do: Copy the .glb into your project folder; glTF 2.0 is Godot's recommended 3D format and imports natively.
Select it in the FileSystem dock, then set Root Scale, Generate LODs and Ensure Tangents in the Import dock and click Reimport.
Double-click the file for the Advanced Import Settings window.
steps.see: An imported scene you can drag straight into the 3D view.
steps.gotcha: Import settings don't change the source file, so fix geometry problems in Blender instead.
